claims.statement: A non-verified receipt can now record a verification command that failed, and the living-documents goal's Outcome no longer overstates where staleness bites. VERIFIED at this commit: --failed-verification COMMAND EXIT_CODE serializes result fail with the observed non-zero code, is refused on a verified receipt because the validator requires all-pass there, refuses exit code 0 because validate_evidence_receipts enforces pass iff exit code 0, and refuses a non-integer code; the recorded failure passes the validator. Before this commit every --verification-command was serialized as result pass with exit_code 0 regardless of status, so an unverified receipt, whose purpose is a proof that could not be reproduced, would have recorded that failure as a pass. VERIFIED by reading the goal against itself: the Outcome claimed a lapse cannot reach main unnoticed while a later paragraph in the same file states that completed checks stay green and only the next push or re-run fails, so a pull request that passes before a review date and merges after it carries the lapse to main; the Outcome now states the narrower behaviour and names the hole. VERIFIED at this commit: 185 tests pass under Python 3.12, scripts/validate.sh reports all executed checks passed with zizmor finding nothing at 24 ignored, and validate_living_docs.py --strict reports 4 documents and 0 stale. UNKNOWN: whether merge-time freshness enforcement is wanted, which is an open owner decision recorded on the roadmap and not decided here.

commands.command: uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -m unittest discover -s tests
